messages:
jo: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing an explicit "eviction" contract for sticky binds when a canary needs to be rolled back. Problem we've hit: session affinity + long tails = canary lives on despite controller wanting full failover. Looking for design alternatives.

liam: Big +1. Two knobs: 1) eviction semantics (soft/evict-now/evict-probabilistic) and 2) eviction lease (how long routers keep the old bind before forcing reassign).

sara: we should also consider a bucketed approach: only evict a percentage of sticky binds per minute to reduce sudden cache churn. Call it "gradual-evict".

jo: sketch of actions:
- PASS: keep routing to current variant (no change)
- DIVERT: assign new binds to target variant, keep sticky binds until finish
- EVICT_GRADUAL: probabilistically reassign a fraction f of sticky binds per minute
- EVICT_IMMEDIATE: refuse old binds for new attaches (do not terminate existing streams)

audrey: critical note: EVICT_IMMEDIATE must not forcibly kill in-flight streams. It only affects new attach attempts and new connections. Also need per-tenant cap so heavy-tail tenants don't stall rollback.

liam: propose decision envelope so routers can operate offline:

```json
{ "decision_id":"d-20260816-007", "tenant":"t-99", "action":"EVICT_GRADUAL", "fraction":0.1, "window_secs":60, "drain_until":5753013000, "ttl_secs":45, "signer":"arbiter-v2", "api_version":"1" }
```

ops-bot: alert: canary c-11 p90 spiked @5753012368

jo: good. Also include reason and metrics_hint: which metric triggered this (e.g., p95_latency, error_rate) so logs show context.

sara: about probabilistic eviction: router needs a stable RNG seed per-tenant so reassignments are reproducible for troubleshooting. Suggest seed = hash(decision_id + router_id).

liam: compatibility labels: some variants have incompatible cache formats. Decision should include per-variant compatibility tag; router refuses to mix incompatible tags unless operator forces. Example: "cache_label":"v2-compat".

audrey: migration plan: 1) implement envelope + local-cache behavior in router behind feature flag; 2) add arbiter to produce envelopes for select tenants; 3) run mirror mode where arbiter writes decisions to controller API and router honors controller; 4) compare diffs for 24-72h; 5) opt-in promotion.

jo: offline/resilience rules:
- If arbiter unreachable, router uses last_signed_decision until ttl expires.
- If ttl expired, router falls back to controller policy and emits rollout_decision_miss metric.
- Routers keep local eviction_counters to avoid oscillation (backoff on flip-flop).

liam: security: sign decisions (JWT) with kid header; include signer info in traces. Also HSM for key rotation.

sara: operator runbook snippet:
1) check decision_id in request traces to find active sticky binds
2) run "rbac-list-binds --tenant t-99 --variant old" to enumerate active binds
3) if active binds > expected, manually trigger EVICT_GRADUAL with higher fraction and observe metric for cache errors
4) if still stuck after N minutes, mark tenant for manual mitigation (drain-friendly restart or user communication)

jo: sample curl to fetch decision for tenant (docs):

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARBITER_TOKEN" \
  https://arbiter.internal/v1/decisions/tenant/t-99 | jq .
```

audrey: metrics: emit rollout_decisions_total{action,tenant,signer} and eviction_applied{tenant,router,action,fraction}. Also rollout_heartbeat per-tenant.

liam: knob tuning: default gradual fraction 0.05, window 60s, min_probe_count 3 OR confidence > 0.9 to escalate to EVICT_IMMEDIATE (manual overrides skip).

ops-bot: note: add alert if decision_miss_count > 10 across fleet in 5m

sara: final thought: support a 'dry-run' flag in the envelope where router logs what it would do but doesn't apply. Useful during migration.

jo: I'll draft RFC with: envelope spec, RNG seeding rules, compatibility labels, migration checklist, runbook steps, and sample metrics/alerts. Posting to #eng-platform for review tomorrow. Thanks all.

liam: :thumbsup: good writeup.
